candidates.name: Search the register
verified_facts: The register search service states that general boundaries are usually available while exact boundaries usually are not recorded.
Online copies can be downloaded but are not proof of ownership; official copies are required for evidential use.
semantic_limits: Search-service output must not be promoted to exact legal-boundary evidence.

candidates.name: Finding information held by HM Land Registry
verified_facts: For unusual addresses or land parcels HM Land Registry directs users to search by map.
If land is unregistered, HM Land Registry may return no ownership result.
semantic_limits: No search result must not be interpreted as a zero-area or zero-height parcel.

candidates.name: Search for land and property information
verified_facts: The title plan provides location and general boundary information.
Downloaded information is not proof of ownership; official copies are required where proof is needed.
semantic_limits: Title-plan general extent is not exact legal-boundary geometry.

candidates.name: About HM Land Registry
verified_facts: HM Land Registry describes a title plan as indicating general boundaries.
HM Land Registry does not provide legal advice on precise boundary positions and responsibilities.
semantic_limits: Institutional scope evidence does not validate parcel terrain values.

candidates.name: Customer Care Review Report and Recommendations 2025
verified_facts: The report distinguishes general boundaries from determined boundaries.
It describes general boundaries as retaining a zone of uncertainty, while determined boundaries identify the exact line once established.
semantic_limits: This review reinforces legal semantics but does not replace the title-specific register evidence.

candidates.name: Practice guide 10: official search of the index map
verified_facts: Plans issued with an index-map search result are for illustrative purposes and do not define the extent of land in an individual title.
The guide warns that title-plan measurements may not match ground measurements because title plans show general boundaries.
semantic_limits: SIM illustrative plans are forbidden as exact parcel polygons.

candidates.name: Practice guide 11: inspection and application for official copies
verified_facts: Official copies of registers and title plans are timed and dated to represent the record at a specific time.
Historical copies of title plans may be available for dates after 13 October 2003 where held electronically.
semantic_limits: Official-copy status and timestamp are legal/lineage evidence, not elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: Your property boundaries: overview
verified_facts: There is usually no record of the exact boundary between two properties.
Most title plans do not show exact boundaries; boundary agreements or determined-boundary applications can record greater precision.
semantic_limits: Ordinary plan evidence remains general-boundary evidence.

candidates.name: Apply to record the exact boundary
verified_facts: An application to record an exact boundary is a determined-boundary application.
The application requires supporting evidence, a DB form and a plan showing the determined boundary prepared with survey input.
semantic_limits: Absence of determined-boundary evidence means exact-line claims remain forbidden.

candidates.name: How to read a title plan
verified_facts: Red edging on a title plan must not be treated as the exact legal boundary.
Measurements scaled from a title plan should not be relied on to locate a legal boundary on the ground.
semantic_limits: Scaled title-plan measurements are excluded from the terrain sampling polygon workflow.

candidates.name: Portal: how to request official copies
verified_facts: Searching by property details only shows title numbers matching the entered details.
HM Land Registry states that other titles affecting the property may not be shown and recommends a search of the index map to find all affecting title numbers.
semantic_limits: A single property-details search is not treated as proof that all intersecting titles were found.

candidates.name: Official copies of register or plan (OC1)
verified_facts: An official copy includes a timestamp and issue date.
The official title plan will likely show only general boundaries rather than exact boundaries.
semantic_limits: Official-copy evidential status does not convert general boundaries into exact geometry.

candidates.name: GeoTIFF 1.1
verified_facts: GeoTIFF 1.1 specifies requirements and encoding rules for georeferenced or geocoded TIFF imagery.
The standard aligns GeoTIFF georeferencing with the EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset.
semantic_limits: GeoTIFF conformance is an encoding/georeference check, not a vertical-accuracy improvement.

candidates.name: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF 1.0
verified_facts: COG uses TIFF tiling, reduced-resolution subfiles, GeoTIFF keys and HTTP range requests.
COG allows applications to retrieve only needed portions of grid coverage data for efficient web access.
semantic_limits: Cloud optimization changes access efficiency, not terrain truth or measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: GeoPackage Encoding Standard
verified_facts: GeoPackage is a portable SQLite container with standard schemas and integrity constraints.
It can store vector features, raster/map tile matrix sets and extensions.
semantic_limits: Container conformance does not turn metadata/index records into elevation observations.

candidates.name: GeoPackage Extension for Tiled Gridded Coverage Data
verified_facts: The extension defines storage of regular gridded coverages such as elevation in GeoPackage.
It supports TIFF-encoded floating-point or integer gridded values and ancillary coverage/tile metadata.
semantic_limits: The project GeoPackage index remains lineage metadata unless it actually contains a declared elevation coverage.

candidates.name: CoverageJSON Community Standard
verified_facts: CoverageJSON defines a JSON format for publishing spatiotemporal coverage data to the Web.
Its design emphasizes lightweight web clients, machine readability and interactive environmental-data applications.
semantic_limits: CoverageJSON representation alone does not validate numeric elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: OGC API - Tiles Standard
verified_facts: OGC API Tiles defines REST building blocks for retrieval of tiled geospatial information.
It can support coverage tiles, map tiles and vector tiles and references Tile Matrix Set metadata.
semantic_limits: A tile service response must be classified as numeric coverage versus rendered map before use.

candidates.name: Two Dimensional Tile Matrix Set and Tile Set Metadata 2.0
verified_facts: TMS 2.0 defines regular tile matrix sets and tile set metadata in a CRS.
Tile set metadata can describe limits, original data and tile matrix linkage.
semantic_limits: Tile indexing and matrix metadata do not add vertical accuracy to contained values.

candidates.name: Web Map Tile Service 1.0
verified_facts: WMTS standardizes serving digital maps as predefined image tiles.
It declares the images a client may request from a server.
semantic_limits: Rendered WMTS map imagery is visual context and is excluded from numeric elevation sampling.

candidates.name: OGC API - Records - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API Records defines resource-centric discovery of metadata records through web APIs.
Records can describe resources such as coverages, tiles, maps, services and assets.
semantic_limits: A metadata record proves discoverability/lineage only, not the underlying elevation value.

candidates.name: OGC API - Maps - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API Maps defines discovery and retrieval of maps independent of the underlying data store.
The standard is map distribution focused and does not itself expose raw coverage values.
semantic_limits: Map API imagery must not be substituted for numeric WCS/GeoTIFF elevation data.
